id_requirements: Two forms of ID are required. Primary ID must be government-issued, include candidate's name, photo, and signature (e.g. passport, driver's license). Secondary ID must include candidate's name and signature or name and photo.
exam_rules: No notes, scratch paper, electronic devices, books, or study materials permitted. Personal items must be stored. No food or drink except water. Restroom breaks allowed but timer continues. Testing center staff may monitor via video/audio.
renewal_options: Earn CE credits through CompTIA CE program (training, conferences, publishing, teaching, higher certs) or retake the current exam version before expiry.

retake_policy.notes: No waiting period required before first retake. After the second failed attempt, candidates must wait 14 calendar days before any subsequent attempt. No limit on total attempts.

editorial.meta_description: The CompTIA Cloud Essentials+ CLO-002 exam is officially retired by CompTIA, and there is no successor exam available for candidates to pursue at this time.
editorial.overview: CompTIA Cloud Essentials+ CLO-002 covered essential cloud concepts, business principles, management, and security. This exam, administered by CompTIA, is now retired. Because the registry names no successor, candidates should consult the official CompTIA website to identify current certification options that align with their professional goals. This retired exam previously served as a baseline for understanding cloud environments and their operational requirements, providing a core knowledge base for individuals entering the IT industry or seeking to understand the broader implications of cloud computing in a modern business environment.
editorial.who_should_take: This retired exam was intended for individuals seeking to understand cloud computing from a business and technical perspective. It was suitable for professionals in management, sales, or technical roles who required a broad overview of cloud service models and deployment strategies to support their organizational objectives.
skills_summary: Analyzing business principles of cloud environments
editorial.preparation_strategy: Since CLO-002 is retired and has no successor, you should not prepare for this exam. Focus your efforts on identifying current, active certifications offered by CompTIA that match your career path. Any knowledge of cloud service models and deployment strategies gained previously remains useful, but you must verify current industry standards and requirements directly through official CompTIA documentation to ensure your skills remain relevant in the evolving technology landscape.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the core concepts of cloud computing, including definitions, characteristics, and various deployment models. It provides the necessary baseline for understanding how cloud environments function and how they differ from traditional on-premises infrastructure solutions in a professional setting.

This domain addresses the business principles and financial considerations of operating within cloud environments. It focuses on the value proposition of cloud adoption, cost management strategies, and the alignment of technical cloud resources with broader organizational goals and financial planning requirements.

This domain focuses on the management and technical operations required to maintain cloud services effectively. It covers the essential tasks needed to ensure that cloud resources are deployed, monitored, and optimized to meet the performance and availability needs of the business organization.

This domain covers governance, risk, compliance, and security practices within the cloud. It details the frameworks and controls necessary to protect sensitive data, ensure regulatory adherence, and manage the inherent risks associated with migrating and maintaining services in a cloud environment.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: As CLO-002 is retired, it cannot be scheduled or taken. You should contact CompTIA to determine if a new certification path is available that meets your professional needs, as no successor exists for this specific exam. Please ensure you are looking at current, active programs.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The retired CLO-002 exam consisted of exactly 75 questions in total. These questions were designed to test a candidate's core knowledge of cloud concepts, business principles, and technical operations within a professional environment before the exam was officially retired by the certifying body.

The passing score for this exam was 720 on a scale of 100-900. This score represented the minimum level of proficiency required to demonstrate a core understanding of cloud computing concepts, business principles, and the management of technical operations within a cloud-based infrastructure environment.

The exam duration was 60 minutes. During this time, candidates were expected to complete the full set of questions provided in the assessment to demonstrate their competency in cloud computing, business principles, and the various technical operations required for successful cloud service management.

The certification remains valid for 3 years from the date of issuance, but renewal is required to maintain active status. Since the exam is now retired, candidates should check with CompTIA regarding their specific certification status and any potential transition paths to current, active industry credentials.
